newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian registrar calls for more share issues.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian registrar calls for more share issues.

text.p: Slovenian central securities registration body KDD appealed on Wednesday to some 260 companies not to hesitate in issuing shares and said it planned a drive to educate firms.
"We think that many companies are not sufficiently informed about how to go about issuing their shares," KDD deputy executive Peter Premk told a news conference.
He said KDD would make more information available on share issues and organise courses on the procedure. The first course will start in March.
"In 1996 we managed to register 203 companies and we expect to reach 500 companies this year," KDD chief executive Boris Snuderl said.
Since June when KDD started electronically registering all transactions on the Ljubljana bourse's primary market it has registered transactions totalling 46 billion tolars ($319.4 million).
KDD expects to receive a U.S. "eligible foreign custodian" licence which would increase its credibility abroad.
"We fulfilled all required conditions last year but all the necessary procedures take some time," Snuderl said.
He said KDD expects Slovenia's largest petrol trader Petrol to register its shares until the end of January.
"Usually shares are listed on the main market two or three months after registering, but it is up to each individual company to decide when it will list its shares," Premk said.
